operating_rules: DECISION-FOCUS CASES beat descriptive cases for journal publication acceptance. Reviewers directly reject descriptive cases. Include problem, protagonist, urgency, decision point.

PROTAGONIST definition: named person (CEO, manager, board member) who must make a choice and face consequences. Must include biographical detail sufficient for reader to understand their perspective (age, background, experience, relevant context).

THREE REQUIRED DATES in case narrative: (1) when problem started, (2) when problem became critical (case positioning date), (3) deadline by which problem must be solved. Creates urgency and frames the teaching scenario.
FREEZE INFORMATION at case problem positioning date. Do not reveal how problem was solved after that date in the narrative. Use epilog section in teaching note for resolution.
PAST TENSE mandatory. All cases written in past tense regardless of recency.

STRUCTURE is flexible but sign-posted. No 'literature review' or 'methodology' sections. Use narrative headings (Problem, Industry Backdrop, Scenario, Dilemma). Writers often incorrectly apply research paper structure, which causes rejection.

TEACHING NOTE prepared during/after case writing, not before. Essential elements: learning objectives (Bloom's taxonomy hierarchy), target audience (be realistic to case problem weight), relevant theory/concepts (pick ONE main focus, not multiple), data collection method, teaching plan (for EMCS: 90 min total: 60 min instruction/debate, 30 min admin).
ASSIGNMENT QUESTIONS must align with learning objective and taught concepts. Place main case problem in final questions to prompt solving/decision-making, not exposition.

TEACHING GUIDE sections are mandatory: synopsis, learning objective, target audience, relevant theory/concepts, data collection method, teaching plan, assignment questions, suggested answers (based only on case narrative info, not external sources), epilog (if applicable).

CONSENT LETTER required only if case uses primary data (interviews). Pure secondary data from publications does not require consent. Controversial cases (ethics, fraud) should get consent even if secondary. Must be from someone with authority to sign.

INTERVIEW flexibility: can interview one person or multiple. Use gatekeeper to access key person. Multiple rounds of interviews acceptable (even after initial submission to address reviewer feedback).
PAIN AND FEAR are the two strongest emotional drivers for human decision-making and behavior change. Personal branding and content strategy built on mirroring audience pain points.

FRAMING/REFRAMING using consequence questions: ask ADBQ (Advantage-Disadvantage-Bad-Question) format to deframe prospects from their current limiting belief. Example: 'How can I communicate you might be making a mistake without you getting upset?' Seeds doubt and lowers guard.

SHEPHERD THE SHEEP (audience leadership): Use 'lead sheep' (first satisfied customer/testimonial) to trigger others to follow. One person taking action causes others to naturally follow. Humans take mental shortcuts by following visible leaders.

OBJECTIONS ARE CONTENT GOLD. Treat prospect objections as inspiration for future content. Find clients who disproved the objection and create case studies/testimonials to address it for 1000s watching.

MISSION-DRIVEN BRAND beats topic-driven brand. Mission = who are you helping + how you transform them. Example: Kanye's mission is self-esteem/self-belief, not music. Apple's mission is creative empowerment, not computers. Allows brand flexibility across products/services.

MOVEMENT building equation: Mission + Community + Action = Movement. Movement bigger than niche. Niche = commoditized. Movement = tribe of believers. 1% conversion of 1M followers = 10K customers vs. 1% of 10K = 100 customers.

AUTHENTICITY AT SCALE: Be so authentically yourself that AI/copycats cannot replicate you. Your unique combination of beliefs, story, personality, journey = unfakeable differentiation. Information commodity now (ChatGPT available) so implementation + relationship becomes the real value.

STORY AS SALES TOOL: Personal story bypasses logic brain and triggers emotional engagement. Relatable struggle (failure, sacrifice, comeback) builds pre-sold audience. People buy from people they connect with, not just from expertise.

MIRRORING PAIN IN CONTENT: Reflect your younger self's struggles in content. Once you have clients, mirror their specific pain points. People feel content is 'made for them' when you articulate their exact problem.

IDENTITY FRAME: Get audience to reject negative identity and run toward positive one. Example: 'Why would you want to be the executive who never fixes their health and never gets promoted?' Frames identity choice, not just behavior change.
named_methods: ADBQ (Advantage-Disadvantage-Bad-Question): Sales/reframing technique using concern tone to seed doubt and lower prospect's guard via consequence questions.
BLOOM'S TAXONOMY: Hierarchical learning objective framework for case teaching (simple to complex cognitive levels).
DECISION-FOCUS CASE METHOD: Case study approach centered on protagonist's critical choice with problem-solving requirement, not just narrative description.
GATEKEEPER STRATEGY: Use existing relationship/authority figure to gain access to protagonist for case interviews.
LEAD SHEEP CONCEPT: First satisfied customer becomes visible proof, triggering social proof cascade for others.
MISSION + METHOD + MOMENTUM PYRAMID: Framework for building lasting personal brand (mission/vision + unique approach + daily execution).

specific_tactics: Case opening hook: answer WHO (protagonist), WHAT (problem), WHERE (location/context), WHEN (problem onset + deadline), WHY (urgency). Keep short and crunchy.
Epilog section placement: Teaching note only, not case narrative. Reveals actual solution/outcome for discussion in class.
Review feedback handling table: List every reviewer comment on left, detailed response/implementation on right. Show exact page numbers and changes. Avoid 'done' or 'it is done' responses.
Consent letter requirement verification: Check if primary data (interviews) used. If yes = required. If pure secondary = optional (unless controversial).
Teaching note timing: Build 3-4 key components (learning objectives, target audience, theory focus) BEFORE data collection. Full teaching note written after case narrative.
Concern tone seeding: Lower tone voice, use 'I'm concerned for you' language to trigger doubt and openness in sales conversation.
Pain island visualization: Map prospect's current pain on one island, desired future on another island. Show water between them (obstacles). Solution is the boat.
Story structure in content: Include struggle, failure point, recovery, current success. Frame as 'relatable path' not 'unattainable peak'.
Social media feed coherence: Mission + consistent visual/messaging aesthetic. Random feeds signal no clear brand position.
Client documentary format: Mini-case studies of how you helped clients. Video testimonials. Proof of results. Demonstrates 'lead sheep' effect.
Content calendar strategy: Document every objection from sales calls. Turn each into a 1-3 min video addressing that specific objection.
prompts: When evaluating a case manuscript: Is there a clear protagonist who must make a decision? If no, recommend rejection.
For case teaching objectives: What is ONE primary concept students will learn? (Not 3-5 mixed concepts)
For assignment questions: Which question forces students to grapple with the core dilemma/decision?
For sales reframing: 'How can I communicate to you that you might be making a mistake without you getting upset with me?' (triggers deframing + doubt)
For content strategy audit: Does my content reflect MY unique story + mission, or just generic advice in my topic?
For mission discovery: Who am I trying to help and how do I want to transform their lives? (Not: what is my niche?)
For audience follow-through: If 1% of my audience buys, what's my revenue at 100 followers vs. 1,000 vs. 1M?
For product/offer design: What different price points can address different segments of my mission-driven audience? (From $40 to $20,000)

contradictions: NICHE VS. BROAD PARADOX (Patrick Deng): Going niche enabled faster monetization (7 figures in tech sales/NFT niches) but prevented building portable brand loyalty. Being broad (travel vlogging) got 0 traction. Solution: Build movement (broad audience) + mission focus (singular philosophy) + monetization layers (multiple offer tiers), NOT traditional niche depth.

DESCRIPTIVE VS. DECISION-FOCUS (Case Study): Descriptive cases rejected by top journals, reviewers call them 'essays not cases.' Yet descriptive cases good for book chapters + conference papers (if allowed by review committee). Decision-focus required for journal publication, not universally.

PRIMARY VS. SECONDARY DATA (Case Study): Secondary data cases harder to address reviewer feedback (info not available to add). Primary data (interviews) easier to iterate but requires consent letter + complexity. Neither has inherent superiority; depends on case problem + revision willingness.

AUTHENTICITY VS. STRATEGY MANIPULATION: Jeremy Miner/Patrick Deng position psychological sales tactics as 'not manipulative if you deliver value.' User argues pain/consequence questions + social proof = dark psychology but justified by outcome. Ethical framing depends on intent + delivery promise alignment.
weird_gold: BUSKING OUTSIDE THE CASINO joke: When asked 'what happens if business fails,' sales trainer casually says prospect will 'be busking outside the casino.' Reframes business failure as humorous absurdity to trigger emotional stakes.

ESPRESSO METAPHOR (Kanye): 'I'm just the espresso, a shot in the morning to get you going.' Reframes brand/influencer role from authoritarian to enabler. Not saying 'be like me,' saying 'I remind you who you are.'
LEAD SHEEP CLAPPING METAPHOR: One person claps at bad performance, others follow naturally. No alpha sheep, just momentum-building. Applied to testimonials/social proof.

TOILET ISSUE CASE STUDY: Sales training uses digestive/workplace bathroom issue to drill down consequence chain (health > performance > boss firing > unemployment > family suffering). Mundane problem scaled to existential stakes.

THERESA ABANDONED CASE: Author wrote appealing case about bamboo houses (cheap, sustainable, but market didn't buy). Case deemed 'too appealing' to author, withdrew it. Author attachment can kill publication.

TESLA REVIEW BREAKDOWN: Two blind reviewers gave nearly identical feedback (contradictory vs. decision-focus, essay not case) without seeing each other's reviews. Validates decision-focus framework across evaluators.

TEACHING NOTE ORDER MISCONCEPTION: Authors often write full teaching note BEFORE case. Correct sequence is objectives + audience + theory FIRST, then data collection, then narrative, then full teaching note. Most get it backwards.

PROPOSITION AMBIGUITY IN SALES: Jeremy Miner demonstrates how 'I'm concerned for you because...' plants doubt before offering solution. Concern tone alone (no explicit objection) shifts prospect psychology.

PATRICK'S 6-MONTH TURNAROUND FORMULA: Quit job month 0, first client month 1, quit full-time month 2, 7K/month month 6 (Yvonne case). Used to prove speed of movement-based monetization when mission/story clear.

AUTHENTICITY = UNFAKEABLE MOAT: Patrick argues AI/ChatGPT destroyed knowledge monopoly. Information free. Unique story + belief system + personality combo is now the actual product. Can't outsource authenticity.

gates: DECISION-FOCUS TEST: If case lacks protagonist + clear decision point + dilemma, recommend rejection before peer review.
PROTAGONIST ADEQUACY TEST: Does reader have enough biographical context to understand protagonist's perspective? (Depends on topic relevance: OB/HR needs detail; Consumer Behavior needs basics)
DATE COMPLETENESS TEST: Case has three dates (problem started, positioned, deadline) and freezes information at position date.
TENSE CONSISTENCY: All narrative in past tense (not mixed with present/future).
STRUCTURE APPROPRIATENESS: No research paper headings (literature review, methodology). Narrative signposting only.
LEARNING OBJECTIVE ALIGNMENT: Assignment questions test the stated objective. No topic drift.
CONSENT VERIFICATION: Primary data = consent letter required. Controversial case = consent recommended regardless.
TARGET AUDIENCE REALISM: Case problem weight matches target audience level. Complex case = graduate/executive audience. Simple case = undergraduate/entry.
THEORY FOCUS SINGULARITY: One main theory/concept highlighted, not 3-5 mixed concepts.
WORD COUNT FEASIBILITY: Information density fits required word limit (e.g., 7,000 word cases must exclude non-essential detail).
